rules.rule_text: Skirts can move from casual to polished through outerwear. A denim jacket or cardigan relaxes a skirt, a leather jacket or bomber adds edge, and a blazer or tailored coat makes midi and simple skirts more office- or dinner-ready. With fuller midi or maxi skirts, shorter jackets often keep the waist visible; with mini skirts, longer coats can provide useful proportion and seasonal balance.

Leggings and very slim bottoms benefit from outerwear that adds shape or coverage. Oversized blazers, long coats, trenches, bombers, and puffers all work depending on formality; a denim jacket gives an easy casual option. Because the lower half is narrow, slightly roomier outerwear usually creates a balanced silhouette, but the jacket should still end at a purposeful point—hip, mid-thigh, or longline—rather than an awkward in-between length.

rules.rule_text: Jeans can take almost any casual or smart-casual outer layer, but choose the jacket to set the tone. A denim jacket or bomber keeps weekends relaxed, a leather jacket adds edge, a blazer makes dark or straight denim office- or dinner-ready, and a trench or long coat adds polish in cooler weather. With baggy jeans, a shorter or more structured jacket helps restore shape; with skinny jeans, a roomier coat can create useful contrast.

Jeans can support both short jackets and longer outerwear, but the choice changes the silhouette. A trench or long coat makes straight and slim denim feel polished; a cropped bomber or blazer gives wide-leg and baggy jeans more waist definition; a leather jacket adds city edge to almost any wash. For a cleaner outfit, let either the denim wash or the outerwear carry the stronger colour or texture rather than making both compete.

rules.rule_text: Classic handbags and leather handbags suit outerwear with a similarly intentional finish. Blazers, tailored coats, trenches, leather jackets, and cardigan jackets all work; smooth structured bags reinforce polish, while softer leather can relax the same outerwear for daytime. Rather than exact colour matching, coordinate the visual weight and hardware: a very ornate handbag needs quieter outerwear, while a minimal bag can sit comfortably against texture or pattern.

Crossbody and sling bags suit practical outerwear because the strap has to sit comfortably across the jacket. Denim jackets, bombers, field jackets, trenches, and light leather jackets all work; on heavier coats, choose a strap long enough to sit without pulling. If both bag and jacket have many pockets, zips, or hardware, simplify the rest of the outfit so the utility details do not compete.

Shoulder bags, flap bags, and satchels work across casual and polished outerwear. A blazer or trench creates city polish, a leather jacket gives edge, a denim jacket keeps the same bag relaxed, and a tailored coat works for dinner or commuting. Check that the shoulder strap clears the jacket's sleeve and lapel comfortably; a bag that constantly catches on bulky outerwear looks less intentional even if the colours work.

rules.rule_text: Pumps, heels, and wedges work naturally with bags that carry some polish. Shoulder bags and structured top handles suit office or daytime, while clutches and mini bags move the outfit toward dinner and events. The bag does not need to match the shoes exactly; a shared material family, metal tone, or one repeated colour is enough. If the heel is highly embellished, keep the bag cleaner so the accessories do not compete.

Court shoes, pumps, and slingbacks look most coherent with bags that share their clean finish. Structured shoulder bags, top-handles, clutches, and compact totes work for work or dinner; a softer shoulder bag can relax lower heels for daytime. Exact colour matching is unnecessary—matching the level of polish, scale, or hardware is usually more sophisticated than making the shoe and bag identical.

rules.rule_text: Boots support bags with a little visual substance. Shoulder bags, crossbodies, totes, structured handbags, and hobos all work; sleek boots pair more easily with structured bags, while biker or chunky boots can take softer or more casual bags. Repeating leather colour can create cohesion, but it is not required—especially when the outfit already contains several brown, black, or metallic elements.

Boots can support either practical or polished bags, but the bag should acknowledge the boot's visual weight. Chunky, combat, or biker boots work with crossbodies, shoulder bags, totes, and soft hobos for everyday wear; sleek ankle or riding boots can take a more structured shoulder bag or top-handle for city polish. Avoid pairing very rugged boots with a tiny ornate bag unless the contrast is intentional, because the accessory can look visually disconnected.
